C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND.IntentSummary: Make re-pairing an extension id that already holds a live credential a proof-gated, distinct operation: POST /ext/pair gains an optional prior_secret wire field, and a request naming an id with a stored credential is refused without storing or returning any secret unless the presented prior secret matches the stored one constant-time (or a verified trust reset — disable — has provably removed it, after which pairing takes today's fresh path); the release dialog distinguishes replacement from first pairing by naming the already-paired extension and stating that approval replaces its live key, while the debug auto-approve becomes cfg(test)-only so no ordinary build re-keys anything without a user decision; after an approved rebind the previous token is fenced on every incoming route, proven by new rebind regressions that fail before the fix and pass after it, the extended pairing-description unit pin, and the unchanged green capability-gating, disable and stream suites.

T-001.Title: Gate re-pairing on prior-secret proof, distinguish the replacement dialog, and make auto-approval test-only

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: PairRequest gains one additive field in src-tauri/src/m045_ext/live_server.rs: pub prior_secret: Option<String> after protocol_version (Option fields deserialize missing as None, so existing pairers keep today's wire shape and no existing field changes name or meaning). Update the stale handle_pair doc comment (lines 541-545, still saying "for now auto-approves") to describe the rebind gate: pairing an id that holds a stored credential requires the prior secret, an unproven rebind is refused leaving the old key valid, and auto-approval exists only in the test harness.

Insert the rebind gate at the top of handle_pair, before the approval decision: read the stored credential with super::auth::get_secret(&req.extension_id) — on Err log BLOCK_PAIR_CREDENTIAL_LOOKUP_FAILED (ext_id and reason only, never secret material) and return 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR {"error": "pairing state unavailable"} without storing anything, because an unreadable store can never authorize replacing a possibly-live key; compute is_rebind = stored.is_some() and proof = match (&stored, req.prior_secret.as_deref()) { (Some(stored), Some(prior)) => super::auth::constant_time_eq(stored.as_bytes(), prior.as_bytes()), _ => false } (constant-time per auth.rs constant_time_eq; length mismatch returns false without timing or logging the mismatch shape); when is_rebind && !proof log BLOCK_PAIR_REBIND_REFUSED (ext_id only) and return 403 FORBIDDEN {"error": "extension already paired; present the prior secret or disable the extension to reset trust"} — no secret is generated, nothing is stored, no dialog is shown, no event is emitted, and the previous token remains valid; the gate runs identically in debug, release and test builds, before any approval arm, so no user decision or harness flag can override it.

Restructure the approval decision: the auto-approve arm becomes #[cfg(test)] (was #[cfg(debug_assertions)]), keeping the BLOCK_PAIR_AUTO_APPROVE log with its text updated to say the approval is test-harness-only, so outside the Rust test harness no build approves pairing without a decision; the dialog arm becomes #[cfg(not(test))] (compiled in ordinary debug runs and release alike), keeping the rfd MessageDialog shape byte-identical (Info level, OkCancelCustom Allow/Deny, spawn_blocking, unwrap_or(false), denial arm 403 {"error": "user denied pairing request"} unchanged) and choosing the description by rebind state: a fresh pairing keeps pairing_grant_description and its exact C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE wording ("wants to pair with Mark", the per-capability grant lines, the "declares no incoming data routes" fallback) with the declared-capability lookup unchanged, while a proven rebind (is_rebind, proof == true) renders a new pure pub(super) fn pairing_rebind_description(extension_name, extension_id) -> String — carrying the same #[cfg_attr(debug_assertions, allow(dead_code))] as its sibling — whose text names the extension and states the replacement, containing the exact phrases "is already paired with Mark" and "replaces its live key", stating that the previous secret stops working and only the new secret will be accepted, and claiming no capability grant beyond what first pairing would grant. The dialog title, buttons and result handling stay unchanged.

Module hygiene and lineage: live_server.rs CHANGE_SUMMARY gains a dated 2026-11-20 C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND entry and the SCOPE line names the prior-secret rebind gate; RouteCapability gating of the data routes, the first-pairing grant description, authenticate_incoming, the C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH stream identity/epoch fencing, secret generation, store_secret overwrite-on-approval semantics for the fresh path, and the PairResponse shape are untouched; no auth.rs, registry.rs, mod.rs, renderer, manifest, Cargo.toml or dependency change; every START_BLOCK_/END_BLOCK_ marker stays paired and unique; no log line, error body or response ever contains secret material (gate refusals log ext_id only).

T-002.Title: Add the rebind regression family, extend the dialog pin, and prove the rebind regressions fail-before and pass-after

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first proof, recorded in the task evidence: the new tests build PairRequest values through serde_json::from_value (JSON with a "prior_secret" key) rather than struct literals, so they compile against the pre-fix source where serde ignores the unknown field; with the T-001 gate temporarily reverted to the #[cfg(debug_assertions)] auto-approve arm (no commit), the unproven-rebind and auto-approve tests are observed red exactly on the silent re-key (200 + old token dead), then with the gate restored the same tests are green — the spec's rebind-regressions-fail-before-pass-after criterion exercised inside one worktree.

Compile reconciliation without weakening anything: fresh_pair_secret (tests.rs 1234-1244) gains prior_secret: None in its struct literal, and fresh_pairing_restores_access (1246-1282) keeps every assertion unchanged in meaning — its pairs happen after mt_ext_disable (verified secret removal), so they now legitimately traverse the gate as the fresh path; the disable family (1143-1190), enabled_extension_passes_only_declared_capability_routes, the capability matrix, and the stream security family stay untouched and green; assert_old_token_fenced is unchanged.

Add the rebind regression family in src-tauri/src/m045_ext/tests.rs (grouped with the pairing family after pairing_grant_description_names_only_declared_capabilities, each test asserting empty events at every refusal): unproven_rebind_refused_and_previous_token_stays_valid — a fixture holding its injected token, a pair request with prior_secret absent returns 403 with a body containing "already paired" and no shared_secret field, super::auth::get_secret still returns the old token, and the old token still passes its declared-capability route; wrong_prior_secret_rebind_refused — the same refusals with a mismatched prior secret, pinning both constant_time_eq arms (missing and mismatched); approved_rebind_fences_previous_token_on_all_routes — a pair request with the correct prior secret returns 200 with a fresh secret different from the old token, and the old token then receives 401 on /ext/context, /ext/apply, /ext/text-insert and /stream/open (stream_open_fixture) with zero events throughout, while the fresh token passes exactly the declared capability's routes; debug_auto_approve_cannot_replace_live_key — under the test harness the #[cfg(test)] arm approves, yet the unproven rebind is still refused with the old key valid, proving the gate dominates auto-approval and an ordinary debug run can never replace a live key without a decision (the cfg(test)-only gating itself is pinned by the T-001 source shapes, since no unit test can execute cfg(not(test)) code); pair_after_trust_reset_takes_fresh_path — mt_ext_disable with verify_secret_absent proof, re-enable, then pair the same id without any prior secret: 200 fresh-path response with today's PairResponse shape, the fresh secret works on the declared route and the old token is 401, followed by a control re-pair without prior secret that is refused because a credential now exists.

Extend the dialog unit pin to cover the replacement wording: pairing_grant_description_names_only_declared_capabilities keeps every existing first-pairing assertion byte-identical and gains a section pinning pairing_rebind_description — for ("TokMo", "tokmo") the description contains "is already paired with Mark" and "replaces its live key", states the previous secret stops working, and contains none of the four capability grant phrases; the test module gains a doc comment line saying the pairing route pairs only with the prior secret when a credential already exists, so the family's intent reads independently of the implementation.
